 Dated this the 25th day of June, 2015  JUDGMENT

The condition imposed on the petitioner who is conducting a rice mill as per approved permit restricting functioning of the mill between 8 a.m and 6 p.m., the petitioner has come up before this Court.

2. The petitioner is conducting a rice mill which is operating for the past 30 years under the name and style "Aiswarya Rice Mill"
within the jurisdiction of the respondent panchayat.
The petitioner alleges that it has all the requisite and valid licenses from various statutory authorities.

3. The petitioner further alleges that the respondents without considering that there is no statutory provision or any condition in the consents/licence/NOC by various statutory authorities which prescribe any time limit in working the factory of the petitioner and overlooking the fact that the Inspector of Factories and Boilers, Perumbavoor has permitted the petitioner to operate 24 hours in three shifts, have issued Ext.P10 letter to the police stating that the petitioner is only permitted to operate between 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
It is with this background, the petitioner has come up before this Court.
4. Though notice has been served on respondents 1 and 2, they did not turn up.
The learned standing counsel for the third respondent had taken notice.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned standing counsel for the third respondent.

6. Ext.P1 issued by the first respondent under the provisions of the Panchayat Raj Act reveals that the petitioner has permission to conduct the mill with 213 H.P motor and the same is valid upto 31.3.2016.
Ext.P2 is the consent issued by the third respondent which is valid upto 30.6.2015.

3 learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that few terms of Ext.P2 has been subsequently varied as per Ext.P3 order dated 20.7.2-013.

sentences.text: Ext.P4 is the NOC issued by the District Medical Officer which approves the site for installation of 213 HP motor for running the unit which categorically holds that from the public health point of view, there is no possibility of any health hazard.

Ext .P5 is the copy of the NOC issued by the Assistant Divisional Officer, Fire and Rescue Services, Ernakulam and Ext.P6 is the certificate issued by the Inspector of Factories and Boilers, Gr.I, Perumbavoor.
Ext.P7 is the certificate of registration with the Commercial Taxes Department, Government of Kerala.
Ext.P8 is the copy of the licence issued under the Food Safety and Standards Act from the Government of India.

7. The learned counsel for the petitioner would point out that the petitioner company is processing about 5000 metric ton paddy per season and at a time, 24 tons of paddy is processed to manufacture double boiled rice.
It is pointed out that this process takes at least 45 hours to complete.
The first stage of the process is to clean the grains using shakers to remove stone, chaff and other unwanted articles.
Thereafter the grain is first boiled (half boiled) using mild heated water which would take at least 8 hours and thereafter the grains are again boiled by steam boiler.
Then the boiled grains are dried using dryer.
It was pointed out that these dryers are sound insulated heat exchequer which would not create any sound.
Thereafter the grains are hulled and then packed.
According to the petitioner, these processes are continuing in nature and the entire process has to be taken in one stretch.
The factory is situated in the middle of 1.5 acres of land and therefore, the petitioner submits that the same would not create any sound or other pollution.
8. Ext.P9 issued by the Inspector of Factories and Boilders, Perumbavoor would reveal that the petitioner was permitted to operate 24 hours in three shifts.
The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that in the first shift between 8 p.m. to 5 p.m. three operators and eight general workers are working.
During the second and third shifts, two operators each are working in the factory.

9. The petitioner is aggrieved by Ext.P10 letter issued by the Sub Inspector of Police, Kodanadu which was caused to be served by the respondent panchayat restricting the operations between 8 a.m and 6 p.m.
This, according to the petitioner, is against the permission already granted.

As the petitioner cannot complete the full process of making double boiled rice without taking at least 45 hours in a stretch, the entire process of making the double boiled rice is continuing and if it is stopped in between, the same would virtually stall the operation of the petitioner's unit.

In fact, the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act (Issue of Licence to Dangerous and Offensive Traders and Factories)
Rules, 1996 does not permit the panchayat to cause the order like Ext.P10 to be served on the petitioner; it was argued.

sentences.text:
10. It is crucial to note that the petitioner is one of the obligants to the Kerala State Civil Supplies Corporation and if the petitioner is forced to work only during the day time, they would not be able to process the grains as per the agreement executed with the Civil Supplies Corporation.
11.
On a consideration of the entire facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that the petitioner is not entitled to get the reliefs prayed for.
